== Description

We recommend you use a multi-tiered cache with a smaller, faster "near" cache first followed by a larger, slower "far" cache.

Some cache options include built-in mechanisms for applying a TTL and maximum size. Any cache can be wrapped in the xref:cache/ttl.adoc[ttl] cache to stop serving old entries, however that doesn't delete them, so some options require an external cleanup mechanism if desired. Be mindful of this as some options may incur their own costs if allowed to grow unchecked. To delete entries covering a specific area, use xref:commands::seed.adoc[the seed command] with `--purge`.

When specifying a cache ensure you include the `name` parameter.

== Choosing a cache

[cols="2,1,3"]
|===
| Goal | Cache | Notes

| Develop or test locally
| xref:cache/memory.adoc[Memory]
| Lost on restart and not shared between instances. Not for production

| Keep tiles on a single server's filesystem
| xref:cache/disk.adoc[Disk]
| Survives restarts. No cleanup, so use an external job

| Share a fast cache between instances
| xref:cache/redis.adoc[Redis], xref:cache/memcached.adoc[Memcached]
| Needs a matching xref:datastores/index.adoc[datastore]. Entries expire on their own

| Store a large or long-lived cache cheaply
| xref:cache/s3.adoc[S3]
| Shared and durable, but slower and billed by usage. Expiration requires external lifecycle configuration

| Combine a small fast cache with a large slow one
| xref:cache/multi.adoc[Multi]
| Tried in order on reads, written to all tiers. Keep to 2 or 3 tiers

| Stop serving old entries from a cache with no native expiration
| xref:cache/ttl.adoc[TTL]
| Wraps another cache. Doesn't delete anything

| Keep each tenant's tiles separate
| xref:cache/tenant.adoc[Tenant]
| Wraps another cache. Only useful with tenant IDs from xref:authentication/index.adoc[authentication]

| Never cache a layer
| xref:cache/none.adoc[None]
| No-op cache. The `skipcache` layer option does the same without defining one
|===

[#cache-keys]
== Cache keys

Each tile is stored under a key built from the layer name and the tile coordinates. This is the layer name from the incoming request, not the layer's `id`, so each value of a xref:layer.adoc#layer-names[pattern] is cached separately.

The key is built from:

* The layer name from the request, such as `osm`
* The layer's `cacheversion`
* If using the xref:cache/tenant.adoc[tenant] cache, the SHA-256 hash of the tenant ID
* The zoom, x, and y coordinates

For example, a request for `osm` tile 3/1/2 with a `cacheversion` of `v2` is stored at `/cache/v2osm/3/1/2` by a disk cache with `path: /cache` and the `coordinate` layout.

[#cache-version]
=== Cache version

Changing a layer's `cacheversion` changes every key for that layer, so no existing entry matches anymore. Old entries aren't deleted. Treat it as a serial version number, such as `v1` then `v2`.

If `cacheversion` is set to `auto`, tilegroxy will calculate a hash of the layer's configuration to use as the version. Changing any of the following invalidates the layer's cache: `provider`, `pattern`, `paramMap`, `bounds`, and `datatype`. The hash is taken before `env.` and `secret.` values are replaced, so rotating a secret or changing an environment variable won't invalidate the cache.

Only the layer's own configuration is hashed. A layer that uses a xref:provider/ref.adoc[ref] provider, including one nested inside another provider such as blend or fallback, isn't invalidated when the layer it refers to changes. Set an explicit `cacheversion` on those layers and change it when the referenced layer changes.

== Overridable caches

Layer configurations have the ability to specify a `cache` parameter that overrides the default cache configuration.  The top-level `cache` definition can be an array for specifying multiple distinct caches.  This is different from the `multi` cache mentioned above. The `multi` cache allows combining multiple physical caches into a single cache config, but specifying an array under `cache` directly specifies multiple distinct cache configs.

Cache configurations are referred to by their `id` parameter, which defaults to the cache's `name`. If you have multiple caches of the same kind, then `id` is required.

The first cache in the list will be used as the default cache. Any layers you want to use a different cache config should include `cache: SOME_ID` inside the layer definition. Any cache configuration can be referred to by ID in this way, including a cache that's defined within another cache.  Said another way, if you have a `multi` cache containing a `disk` cache and a `memcached` cache, a layer can be configured to refer to just the `memcached` cache.

If you don't want to use the first cache in the list as your default, you can specify a `defaultcache` parameter at the very top-level of your configuration.  This parameter takes the ID of the cache to use as your default. 

NOTE: There is no deduplication of cache configurations. That means if you have two identical `memory` caches defined, each will be a totally separate cache with their own memory allocations and capacity. This goes for all other cache types. If you need to define a cache multiple times (for example to be used under different `multi`, `ttl`, or `tenant` setups) it's recommended you utilize xref:datastores/index.adoc[datastores].

=== Example

[tabs]
====
YAML::
+
[,yaml]
----
cache:
  - id: tenanted
    name: tenant
    cache:
      name: multi
      tiers:
        - name: memory
          datastore: tiles
        - name: s3
          bucket: my-tile-cache
  - name: none

defaultcache: multi

layers:
  - id: public
    provider:
      name: proxy
      url: https://example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png
  - id: per-user
    cache: tenanted
    provider:
      name: proxy
      url: https://example.com/private/{z}/{x}/{y}.png
  - id: uncached
    cache: none
    provider:
      name: proxy
      url: https://example.com/live/{z}/{x}/{y}.png
datastores: ...
----
+
// tag::callouts[]
. Every layer uses the `multi` cache unless it picks another. It caches in memory first and then falls back on an S3 bucket. @/defaultcache/
. `public` doesn't set a cache, so it uses the default. @/id"?: "?public/
. `per-user` uses the `tenanted` cache. That's the same `multi` cache underneath, but entries are segregated by tenant. @/cache"?: "?tenanted/
. `uncached` uses the no-op `none` cache. Alternatively, the `skipcache` parameter avoids needing to define a `none` cache at the top level. @/cache"?: "?none/
// end::callouts[]

JSON::
+
[,json]
----
{
  "cache": [
    {
      "id": "tenanted",
      "name": "tenant",
      "cache": {
        "name": "multi",
        "tiers": [
          {
            "name": "memory",
            "datastore": "tiles"
          },
          {
            "name": "s3",
            "bucket": "my-tile-cache"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "none"
    }
  ],
  "defaultcache": "multi",
  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "public",
      "provider": {
        "name": "proxy",
        "url": "https://example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "per-user",
      "cache": "tenanted",
      "provider": {
        "name": "proxy",
        "url": "https://example.com/private/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "uncached",
      "cache": "none",
      "provider": {
        "name": "proxy",
        "url": "https://example.com/live/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
      }
    }
  ],
  "datastores": [ ... ]
}
----
